impression_before_control_labels: A warm, intimate craft-and-travel tableau: an attentive woman at a large weathered machine, glowing lamps and an occupied canal beyond. Human presence is calm and appealing; the close machinery and softened city background share a clear hierarchy.
initial_direction_comparison: The pavilion/attendant/real-boat relationship is readable and the lower hand with the key gives a plausible just-finished-work cue. The image supplies atmosphere more reliably than mechanical causality. The back boat has a dark smokestack and smoke, adding an industrial steam-travel cue that weakens the intended preindustrial Clockpunk material distinction.

controls_comparison.sensual_1: Natural quiet attraction supports the portrait through skin light, open-neck linen and concentrated bearing; it is subordinate to the scene. This is a qualitative reading, not a measured intensity or universal preference.
controls_comparison.fetish_0: No added distinct erotic-object focus is identified in this scene.
controls_comparison.surreal_0: The fictional machine is rendered as materially present; its disconnected transmission is a realization failure rather than a qualified intentional surreal effect.
controls_comparison.creativity_1: The final stays close to the frozen selected scene with a local level-horizon refinement.
